events.title: Kingdom of Ebla
events.description: Ebla in northern Syria became an important city-state controlling trade routes. Ebla's archive tablets recorded rich economic, political and diplomatic information, important for understanding the ancient Near East. Ebla used cuneiform script and Semitic language.

events.title: Phoenician City-States Flourish
events.description: Phoenician city-states on Syrian coast (including modern Lebanon) like Ugarit and Arwad flourished. Phoenicians were great sailors and merchants, invented alphabetic writing, profoundly influencing Greek and Western civilization.

events.title: Assyrian Conquest of Syria
events.description: Assyrian Empire conquered Syrian Aramaic kingdoms, incorporating Damascus. Aramaic became lingua franca of Near East for millennia. Syria became strategic battleground for empires like Assyria, Neo-Babylon and Persia.

events.title: Alexander's Conquest of Syria
events.description: Alexander the Great defeated Persia at Battle of Issus, conquering Syria. He besieged and captured Tyre on Mediterranean coast. Syria entered Hellenistic period, Greek culture merged with local culture.

events.title: Seleucid Dynasty Rule
events.description: Seleucus I established Seleucid Empire, Syria became its core territory. He founded Antioch as capital, city became important center of Hellenistic world. Seleucid rule promoted Greco-Near Eastern cultural exchange.

events.title: Roman Conquest of Syria
events.description: Roman general Pompey conquered Seleucid remnants, Syria became Roman province. Roman rule brought over 200 years of peace and prosperity to Syria. Cities like Palmyra, Damascus and Antioch flourished.

events.title: Palmyra's Prosperity
events.description: Desert oasis city Palmyra (Tadmur) controlled East-West trade routes, becoming wealthy commercial center. Palmyra blended Greco-Roman and Near Eastern culture, left magnificent ruins.

events.title: Queen Zenobia's Rule
events.description: Palmyra Queen Zenobia ruled after husband's assassination, conquered Syria, Egypt and parts of Asia Minor, challenging Roman authority. But Roman Emperor Aurelian defeated and captured her, destroyed Palmyra. Zenobia became legendary figure.

events.title: Byzantine Christian Period
events.description: Syria became part of Byzantine Empire after Roman Empire split. Christianity dominated, Syria became center of theological debate and monastic movement. Multiple Christian sects flourished, including Syriac Christianity which preserved ancient knowledge.

events.title: Battle of Yarmouk and Arab Conquest
events.description: Arab Muslims defeated Byzantines at the Yarmouk River, conquering Syria. Damascus surrendered, becoming an important city under Islamic rule. Syria gradually Islamized and Arabized, but Christian and other religious communities continue to this day.

events.title: Umayyad Caliphate
events.description: The Umayyad family established a caliphate with Damascus as capital. This was Damascus's golden age as capital of the Islamic world. Umayyad Caliphs conquered vast territories from Spain to India. The Umayyad Mosque in Damascus was built during this period, becoming an Islamic architectural masterpiece.

events.title: Saladin and Battle of Hattin
events.description: Saladin defeated the Crusaders at Hattin, recapturing Jerusalem. Saladin unified Egypt, Syria and Mesopotamia, establishing the Ayyubid dynasty. He was known for chivalry and tolerance, respected even in the West.

events.title: Battle of Ain Jalut
events.description: Mamluks defeated Mongols at Ain Jalut in Palestine, halting Mongol advance. This was first major Mongol defeat. Mamluks then conquered Syria, ending Ayyubid and Mongol threats. Damascus became an important Mamluk city.

events.title: Timur Destroys Damascus
events.description: Timur's army captured and sacked Damascus, massacring inhabitants, destroying city. Timur deported Damascus's craftsmen to Samarkand. Damascus took decades to recover from this disaster.

events.title: Ottoman Conquest of Syria
events.description: Ottoman Sultan Selim I defeated the Mamluks at Marj Dabiq, conquering Syria. Syria became an Ottoman province for 400 years. Ottoman rule brought stability to Syria, but also a period of decline.

events.title: Egyptian Occupation
events.description: Egyptian governor Muhammad Ali conquered Syria, implementing modernization reforms. His rule was harsh, imposing heavy taxes and conscription. European powers intervened, forced Egypt to withdraw, Ottoman rule restored.

events.title: Damascus Massacre
events.description: Sectarian violence erupted in Damascus, thousands of Christians massacred by Muslims. European powers, especially France, intervened. Massacre was part of broader Mount Lebanon sectarian conflict.

events.title: Sykes-Picot Agreement
events.description: Britain and France secretly agreed to divide Ottoman Arab lands. Syria allocated to France. This agreement betrayed Arab national aspirations, causing lasting resentment in Arab world.

events.title: Arab Army Enters Damascus
events.description: Faisal's Arab forces with British support captured Damascus from Ottomans. Arabs celebrated, hoped for independent Arab state. But European powers had other plans.

events.title: Syrian Arab Kingdom
events.description: Syrian National Congress declared Faisal king of united Syrian kingdom (including Lebanon, Palestine, Jordan). But this kingdom was short-lived, France refused to recognize it.

events.title: Battle of Maysalun and French Occupation
events.description: French forces defeated Syrian army at Maysalun, captured Damascus. Faisal expelled, Syria became French mandate. French divided Syria, created Lebanon, Alawite and Druze states. This period left deep scars in Syrian national consciousness.

events.title: Great Syrian Revolt
events.description: Druze leader Sultan al-Atrash led large-scale revolt against French. Revolt spread nationwide, French brutally suppressed, bombed Damascus. Though revolt failed, it became symbol of Syrian resistance.

events.title: Franco-Syrian Treaty
events.description: France and Syrian nationalists signed treaty promising independence, but France never ratified it. Treaty failure frustrated Syrian nationalists.

events.title: British and Free French Invasion
events.description: Britain and Free France invaded Vichy-controlled Syria, ending Vichy rule. Free France promised Syrian independence but delayed.

events.title: Syrian Independence
events.description: The last French soldier left Syria, Syria gained full independence. April 17 became National Day. But the new nation faced political instability, economic difficulties and Israeli threats.

events.title: First Arab-Israeli War
events.description: Syria joined other Arab states in war against Israel. Syria was defeated, lost territory. War created Palestinian refugee crisis, brought military's prestige into question, triggered political instability.

events.title: Husni al-Zaim Coup
events.description: Colonel Husni al-Zaim launched first military coup in modern Arab history. Al-Zaim ruled briefly but was soon overthrown and executed. This began Syria's era of coups and political chaos.

events.title: Union with Egypt
events.description: Syria and Egypt formed United Arab Republic under Nasser. Merger aimed to realize pan-Arab unity dream. But Egyptian domination and socialist policies dissatisfied Syrians, Syria seceded in 1961.

events.title: Ba'ath Party Seizes Power
events.description: Ba'ath Party launched coup, seizing power. Ba'athism advocated pan-Arab socialism. Though Ba'ath theoretically ruled, actual power was controlled by military officers and Alawite clique.

events.title: Six-Day War and Loss of Golan Heights
events.description: Israel preemptively attacked Arab states, Syria lost Golan Heights. This humiliating defeat traumatized Syrians, intensified anti-Israeli sentiment. Golan issue remains unresolved.

events.title: Hafez al-Assad's Coup
events.description: Defense Minister Hafez al-Assad launched the 'Corrective Movement' coup, seizing power. Assad established personal dictatorship, ruling Syria for 30 years. He relied on the minority Alawite sect and security apparatus, brutally suppressing dissent.

events.title: Yom Kippur War
events.description: Syria and Egypt launched surprise attack on Israel. Initially successful, but Israel counterattacked, pushed deeper into Syrian territory. Though war ended in stalemate, Syria failed to recapture Golan. War reinforced Assad's military regime.

events.title: Intervention in Lebanese Civil War
events.description: Syria sent troops to Lebanon to intervene in civil war. Syria became dominant force in Lebanon, occupying until 2005. Lebanon intervention became key part of Assad's regional strategy but also costly burden.

events.title: Hama Massacre
events.description: The Muslim Brotherhood rebelled in Hama, Assad ordered the military to crush it, leveling parts of the city, killing 10,000-40,000 civilians. This massacre eliminated Islamic opposition, demonstrated regime brutality, plunging Syria into fearful silence for 20 years.

events.title: Participation in Gulf War Coalition
events.description: Syria joined US-led coalition against Iraq in Gulf War. This surprising move earned Assad international rehabilitation and strengthened grip on Lebanon. Syria received significant financial aid from Gulf states.

events.title: Death of Hafez al-Assad
events.description: Hafez al-Assad died after 30 years of rule. His son Bashar al-Assad succeeded as president. Bashar was initially seen as a reformer, people hoped for a 'Damascus Spring,' but hopes were soon dashed.

events.title: Withdrawal from Lebanon
events.description: After Hariri assassination in Lebanon blamed on Syria, massive protests and international pressure forced Syria to withdraw troops from Lebanon, ending 29-year occupation. This was major setback for Assad regime.

events.title: Syrian Uprising Begins
events.description: Inspired by the 'Arab Spring,' people in southern Deraa protested, demanding reforms and release of arrested children. Regime violence triggered nationwide protests. Peaceful demonstrations gradually evolved into armed uprising and devastating civil war.

events.title: Militarization of Uprising
events.description: Peaceful protests gradually turned into armed conflict. Defecting soldiers formed Free Syrian Army (FSA). Regime used tanks and artillery against cities. Thousands died, hundreds of thousands displaced. International community condemned but failed to stop violence.

events.title: Ghouta Chemical Attack
events.description: Chemical weapons attack in Damascus suburbs killed hundreds of civilians. International community widely blamed Assad regime. US threatened military action but Russia brokered deal for Syria to surrender chemical weapons. Attack crossed 'red line' but brought no serious consequences for Assad.

events.title: Rise of Islamic State
events.description: ISIS rapidly expanded in Syria, capturing Raqqa as 'capital.' ISIS brutality shocked world, beheading hostages, enslaving Yazidis. ISIS complicated Syrian conflict, making international intervention difficult, as West feared strengthening Islamist extremists.

events.title: Russian Military Intervention
events.description: As Assad's regime neared collapse, Russia launched massive airstrikes supporting government forces. Russian intervention was the war's turning point, reversing battlefield situation, giving Assad the upper hand again.

events.title: Fall of Aleppo
events.description: Government forces with Russian and Iranian support recaptured Aleppo, the opposition's largest stronghold. The city suffered brutal siege and bombardment, thousands of civilians died. Aleppo's fall marked a major defeat for the opposition.

events.title: ISIS Defeated
events.description: US-backed Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) captured Raqqa, ISIS's 'capital.' Russian-backed regime forces cleared ISIS from central Syria. Though ISIS 'caliphate' collapsed, remnants continue guerrilla warfare.

events.title: Eastern Ghouta and Douma Chemical Attack
events.description: Assad regime recaptured Eastern Ghouta near Damascus with brutal offensive. Chemical attack in Douma killed dozens. US, UK and France launched limited missile strikes against Syrian chemical facilities. But attacks had little impact on war.

events.title: Turkish Invasion of Northeast
events.description: After US withdrew troops, Turkey invaded northeast Syria attacking Kurdish forces. Turkey aimed to create 'safe zone,' resettle Syrian refugees. Kurds felt betrayed by US, turned to Assad and Russia for protection.

events.title: Idlib Crisis
events.description: Assad regime and Russia attacked last major opposition stronghold Idlib. Offensive created humanitarian disaster, hundreds of thousands fled toward Turkish border. Turkey intervened militarily, Russia and Turkey reached ceasefire.

events.title: Caesar Act Sanctions
events.description: US implemented Caesar Act, imposing harsh sanctions on Assad regime and supporters. Sanctions aimed to pressure regime, cut off reconstruction funding. Sanctions worsened Syria's economic crisis, ordinary people suffered most.

events.title: Major Earthquake Disaster
events.description: Devastating 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck Turkey-Syria border, killing over 50,000 in Turkey and 6,000 in Syria. Syrian northwest was worst hit, rescue hampered by war and sanctions. Earthquake worsened Syria's humanitarian crisis.

events.title: Arab States Reconcile with Assad
events.description: Saudi Arabia and other Arab states restored relations with Assad's regime, Syria rejoined the Arab League. This marked international community abandoning efforts to overthrow Assad, the Assad regime survived.

events.title: Stalemate and Ongoing Suffering
events.description: Syria's civil war entered stalemate stage. Assad controls most territory but the economy collapsed. Syria is divided into multiple control zones: government, Turkish-backed opposition, Kurdish autonomous region. 500,000 dead, 12 million displaced, the country in ruins. Prospects for reconstruction and reconciliation are bleak.

events.title: 大地震災難
events.description: 土耳其-敘利亞邊境發生7.8級地震,敘利亞西北部受災嚴重,超過6000人死亡。政權控制區和反對派控制區都受影響。國際援助困難,人道危機加劇。...

events.title: 阿拉伯國家與阿薩德和解
events.description: 沙特阿拉伯等阿拉伯國家與阿薩德政權恢復關係,敘利亞重返阿拉伯國家聯盟。這標誌著國際社會放棄推翻阿薩德的努力,阿薩德政權存活下來。...

events.title: 僵局與持續苦難
events.description: 敘利亞內戰進入僵局階段。阿薩德控制大部分領土但經濟崩潰。敘利亞分裂為多個控制區:政府、土耳其支持的反對派、庫爾德自治區。50萬人死亡,1200萬人流離失所,國家...
